title: Fix the task validation in agent service (10X efficiency!)
body:
Fixes Issue identified by @mahlertom in issue https://github.com/gregpr07/browser-use/issues/56. 

The issue adresses the problem with the function `get_next_action` in `Agent` where the AI invoke does not fully understand that it completed a task and does not ultimately call the `done` action. 
**It actually became much more efficient in solving some tasks!**
Instead of being stuck in a loop, it understands whether or not it has already solved a given task and continues running.

In order to solve this problem, I have inserted a prompt into the end of `input_messages` that emphasizes the agent's task and reminds it to call `done` when completed. 
I have tested it on the code that @mahlertom submitted and on dosens of my own tests over the past weeks since I opened the PR - it works perfectly. 

Cheers.

title: [BUG] `on_page` is called not being called for the first `new_page()` in `_initialize_session`
body:
# Summary
Addressing issue https://github.com/browser-use/browser-use/issues/114/
When running `async def _initialize_session(self)` in `browser_use/browser/context.py` the method: `self._add_new_page_listener(context)` is called at the end, after page was already created.
Therefore, the `on_page` in `_add_new_page_listener` is not triggered for that page, only for later pages.

Also, I noticed that `_add_new_page_listener` does not have to be async.

To fix that, I moved the call for `_add_new_page_listener` above the page creation.

# Testing and Reproduction:

To reproduce, put a breakpoint inside `on_page` inside `_add_new_page_listener`, and another breakpoint after the line `page = await context.new_page()` in `_initialize_session`.
You will see that `on_page` is not triggered.

Then apply the fix I made, and retry, to see that the `on_page` not correctly triggers.

I used the example from issue https://github.com/browser-use/browser-use/issues/114/ and now I can see my `print()`:


```python
import asyncio

from langchain_openai import ChatOpenAI
from playwright.async_api import (
	BrowserContext as PlaywrightBrowserContext,
)
from playwright.async_api import Page

from browser_use import Agent, Browser, BrowserConfig
from browser_use.browser.context import BrowserContext


class MyBrowserContext(BrowserContext):
	def _add_new_page_listener(self, context: PlaywrightBrowserContext):
		async def on_page(page: Page):
			# My implementation for on_page to allow for custom logic
			print(page.url)

		context.on('page', on_page)


async def main():
	browser = Browser(config=BrowserConfig(headless=True))
	browser_context = MyBrowserContext(browser=browser)
	agent = Agent(
		task='Find a one-way flight from Bali to Oman on 12 January 2025 on Google Flights. Return me the cheapest option.',
		llm=ChatOpenAI(model='gpt-4o-mini'),
		browser=browser,
		browser_context=browser_context,
	)
	await agent.run()

asyncio.run(main())
```

title: Fix: Remove large file from Git history and implement Git LFS for test data
body:
Fixes: #102 

The main issue was that the file `tests/mind2web_data/processed.json` was directly committed to the Git history, causing the repository to be large and slow to clone.

To resolve this, I took the following steps:

1. **Removed `tests/mind2web_data/processed.json` from the Git history:** I used the `git filter-repo` tool to rewrite the history and remove this file from all past commits. This significantly reduces the repository size and improves cloning speed.

2. **Implemented Git LFS for `tests/mind2web_data/processed.json`:**  To ensure that this file (and any future large files) are managed efficiently, I have added it to Git Large File Storage (LFS). This means that the actual file content is stored separately, and Git only tracks a small pointer in the repository.

- The `.gitattributes` file was updated to track `tests/mind2web_data/processed.json` with LFS.
- The `tests/mind2web_data/processed.json` file itself now contains the Git LFS pointer.

**Important Note Regarding Force-Push:**

Rewriting Git history to remove the large file required a force-push. This force-push was performed on my forked repository during the history rewriting process. The current state of the `remove-large-file-from-git-history` branch reflects this rewritten history.

title: Fix: react handlers do not handle existing select implementation
body:
The current implementation of `Controller.select_dropdown_option` does not handle React applications well. Current implementation dispatches a "change" event on the select element. This is generally okay, but react does not attach listeners directly to the DOM elements. Instead react has listeners on the root element, and every event is expected to bubble to the root element for it to be handled. 

I have added `bubbles: true` to fix this issue.

Fixes issue described in #163  (have created a basic test case as well)

**EDIT [2024-05-07 11:18 IST]:** Just adding bubbles:true still did not work for few React websites (example: https://www.autotrader.co.uk/). Replaced the implementation with Playwright's [select_option()](https://playwright.dev/docs/api/class-locator#locator-select-option). This seems to work across frameworks as far as I have tested.

title: feature: Support CDP_URL in BrowserConfig
body:
This pull request introduces support for connecting to remote browsers using the Chrome DevTools Protocol (CDP). 
A new `cdp_url` parameter has been added to the `BrowserConfig` class, enabling users to specify a custom CDP endpoint for use with tools like `headless-shell` or `browserless`.

### **Key Changes**
- Added `cdp_url` as an optional parameter to the `BrowserConfig` class.
- Updated the `Browser._setup_browser` method to handle CDP connections via the `cdp_url` parameter.
- Added a new example script, `using_cdp.py`, to demonstrate how to connect to a CDP-enabled browser instance.

### **How to Test**
1. **Set up Chrome for CDP**:
   - Start Chrome with the `--remote-debugging-port=9222` flag.
   - Verify that the endpoint is active by visiting `http://localhost:9222/json/version` in your browser.
2. **Run the Example Script**:
   - Use the provided `using_cdp.py` script.
   - Ensure the `GEMINI_API_KEY` environment variable is set (if applicable).
   - Observe successful connection to the browser instance via CDP.

### **Why**
#189

title: Fix for nested iframes
body:
Fixes #295, needs to be tested.

**The solution:**

1. Removed the break condition when finding an iframe parent. This allows us to collect all iframe parents in the hierarchy.
2. Reversed the parents list to process them from top to bottom (outermost to innermost iframe).
3. Changed the logic to process all iframe parents in sequence, rather than just the first one.
4. Renamed variables for better clarity (iframe_parent → iframes).

**Changes:**

- Previously, we were breaking after finding the first iframe parent and only processing that one
- Now we collect all iframe parents and process them in sequence from outermost to innermost
- Each iframe parent creates a new frame locator that we chain together to reach the target element

This should now properly handle multiple levels of iframe nesting.

# Add Discord Bot Integration with Browser-Use
## Overview
This PR introduces a new DiscordBot API for integrating a Discord bot with Browser-Use to run it by triggering it directly through messages. It handles the messages asynchronously and replies to the corresponding messages with the result.

## Key Features
-  Complete Discord bot API integration with Browser-Use tool
-  Comprehensive documentation for understanding the usage.
-  Robust error handling, delivers a receipt if something goes wrong.
-  Message context preservation (replies to the triggering/corresponding message)
-  User pinging functionality for better notification flow
-  Configurable API settings for flexible use e.g. changing the prefix, headless mode and other browser configs.
-  Comprehensive instructions to setup a bot and demonstration of DiscordBot API usage in discord_example.py 

## Demonstration 
- Comprehensive instructions to setup a Discord Bot into a Server are provided in /examples/discord_example.py 
- Example use of DiscordBot is demonstrated with comments in discord_example.py

title: Fix incorrect import of BrowserContext in documentation example
body:
### Description  
This PR fixes an incorrect import statement in the documentation example for reusing an existing browser instance. The current example imports `BrowserContext` from `playwright.async_api`, but it should be imported from `browser_use.browser.context` to align with the design of the `browser_use` library.

### Changes Made  
- Updated the sample code in the documentation to replace:
  ```python
  from playwright.async_api import BrowserContext
  ```
  with:
  ```python
  from browser_use.browser.context import BrowserContext
  ```
### Why this change is necessary  
The incorrect import may cause confusion or lead to unintended behavior when users follow the documentation. Using the correct `BrowserContext` ensures consistency with the library's intended usage and leverages its full capabilities.  

Let me know if you'd like any refinements to this text!

title: Solving the installation issue #441
body:
Fix Python version compatibility issue

Updated the Python version constraint in pyproject.toml from ">=3.11" to ">=3.11,<4.0" to resolve dependency conflicts with langchain-google-genai which requires Python <4.0.

This change:
- Maintains the minimum Python requirement of 3.11
- Adds an upper bound of Python <4.0
- Resolves poetry install failures due to version incompatibility
- Ensures compatibility with all project dependencies

The error was occurring because langchain-google-genai requires Python <4.0, but our project didn't specify an upper bound for the Python version.

title: Extend custom functions with user interaction and advanced browser interactions
body:
Add new functions for user interaction and advanced browser interactions.

* **User Interaction Functions**
  - Add `ask_for_user_input` function to prompt the user for input and return the response.
  - Add `display_notification` function to show notifications to the user.
  - Register these functions using the `@controller.action` decorator with `requires_browser=True` parameter.

* **Advanced Browser Interaction Functions**
  - Add `handle_file_upload` function to upload files to a website.
  - Add `interact_with_iframes` function to interact with elements inside iframes.
  - Register these functions using the `@controller.action` decorator with `requires_browser=True` parameter.

* **Examples**
  - Create `user_interaction.py` to demonstrate the usage of `ask_for_user_input` and `display_notification` functions.
  - Create `advanced_browser_interactions.py` to demonstrate the usage of `handle_file_upload` and `interact_with_iframes` functions.

title: Option to exclude dynamic css attributes
body:
This pull request introduces a new configuration option to include or exclude dynamic attributes in CSS selectors within the `BrowserContextConfig` class. The changes ensure that the dynamic attributes can be controlled through a configuration setting, improving the flexibility and reusability of CSS selectors.

Key changes include:

### New Configuration Option:

* Added `include_dynamic_attributes` attribute to the `BrowserContextConfig` class to allow toggling the inclusion of dynamic attributes in CSS selectors. [[1]](diffhunk://#diff-02d6625e62a1cd7252a850b065c545a42620cf0aebfc595ccbe51f065aee9947R100-R102) [[2]](diffhunk://#diff-02d6625e62a1cd7252a850b065c545a42620cf0aebfc595ccbe51f065aee9947R127)

### Method Updates:

* Updated the `_enhanced_css_selector_for_element` method to accept an `include_dynamic_attributes` parameter, which controls whether dynamic attributes are included in the generated CSS selector.
* Modified the logic within `_enhanced_css_selector_for_element` to conditionally include dynamic attributes based on the new parameter. [[1]](diffhunk://#diff-02d6625e62a1cd7252a850b065c545a42620cf0aebfc595ccbe51f065aee9947L779-R783) [[2]](diffhunk://#diff-02d6625e62a1cd7252a850b065c545a42620cf0aebfc595ccbe51f065aee9947L800-L804) [[3]](diffhunk://#diff-02d6625e62a1cd7252a850b065c545a42620cf0aebfc595ccbe51f065aee9947L820-R837)

### Integration with Existing Methods:

* Updated the `get_locate_element` method to pass the `include_dynamic_attributes` configuration setting to the `_enhanced_css_selector_for_element` method.

### Message Handling Improvements:

[[1]](diffhunk://#diff-7ae2f2cabb27b60892d2f4ec16bf443d4802dfd72d60129c4decf8e913aaa2deL11-L13) [[2]](diffhunk://#diff-7ae2f2cabb27b60892d2f4ec16bf443d4802dfd72d60129c4decf8e913aaa2deL25-R25) [[3]](diffhunk://#diff-7ae2f2cabb27b60892d2f4ec16bf443d4802dfd72d60129c4decf8e913aaa2deL55-R56) [[4]](diffhunk://#diff-7ae2f2cabb27b60892d2f4ec16bf443d4802dfd72d60129c4decf8e913aaa2deL65-L68) [[5]](diffhunk://#diff-7ae2f2cabb27b60892d2f4ec16bf443d4802dfd72d60129c4decf8e913aaa2deL107-R114) [[6]](diffhunk://#diff-7ae2f2cabb27b60892d2f4ec16bf443d4802dfd72d60129c4decf8e913aaa2deL123-L130)

* Updated element interaction rules to use a more consistent format for interactive and non-interactive elements, ensuring clarity in the prompts. * Moved the step information description to a more appropriate location in the `get_user_message` method. title: Add "wait_for_element" capability.
body:
This PR should add the "wait_for_element" action and initial_action, with the optional timeout which defaults to 10 seconds.

It's useful for lazy-loaded websites, loading overlays or elements that only appears after a certain time. The current behavior is to scroll the page until the element is spotted, and it may miss the desired elements that will be no longer visible after scrolling.

author: MagMueller

title: Check for pause more often
body:
This pull request includes several changes to improve the handling of paused or stopped states in the `browser_use` module. The main focus is on refactoring the code to centralize the check for paused or stopped states and ensuring this check is consistently applied throughout the relevant methods.

Refactoring and state check improvements:

* Added a new method `_check_if_stopped_or_paused` to the `Agent` class in `browser_use/agent/service.py` to centralize the logic for checking if the agent is paused or stopped.
* Replaced individual checks for `_stopped` or `_paused` with calls to the new `_check_if_stopped_or_paused` method in the `step` method of `browser_use/agent/service.py`. [[1]](diffhunk://#diff-3736f406057606f65f3ea79952b7f0ec8f8a22f25a49d7a0771f4cfbf43cbb92L249-R261) [[2]](diffhunk://#diff-3736f406057606f65f3ea79952b7f0ec8f8a22f25a49d7a0771f4cfbf43cbb92L265-R271) [[3]](diffhunk://#diff-3736f406057606f65f3ea79952b7f0ec8f8a22f25a49d7a0771f4cfbf43cbb92R284)
* Updated the `run` method in `browser_use/agent/service.py` to include the new `_check_if_stopped_or_paused` method.
* Modified the `multi_act` method in `browser_use/controller/service.py` to accept a `check_break_if_paused` parameter and call this function at various points to ensure the paused state is checked. [[1]](diffhunk://#diff-af6f6bc87d2d09d2a9f08f03fc959eb25b5637f37e959ec655daeba030ede225R447) [[2]](diffhunk://#diff-af6f6bc87d2d09d2a9f08f03fc959eb25b5637f37e959ec655daeba030ede225R458-R465) [[3]](diffhunk://#diff-af6f6bc87d2d09d2a9f08f03fc959eb25b5637f37e959ec655daeba030ede225R474-R475)

Other changes:

* Updated the import statements in `browser_use/controller/service.py` to include the `Callable` type.
* Changed the task description in the `AgentController` class in `examples/features/pause_agent.py` to open multiple websites in one action.

body:
This PR adds hover and evaluate abilities to browser-use. It's now possible to run javascript functions on webpages (evaluate), which is very useful for scrolling, triggering specific functions or interacting with dynamic elements.

Also adds the hover ability, so it's abe to hover elements.

As a result, for actions that declare a parameter named “browser,” the function call is missing this argument. title: Improve Text Input Handling in Browser Context
body:
## Description
This PR addresses issue #543 where the message box would not accept text input, causing issues with text entry and operator crashes. The changes improve the text input handling in the browser context by adding better state management, error handling, and support for different types of input fields.

## Changes Made
- Enhanced [_input_text_element_node](cci:1://file:///d:/Github/browser-use/browser_use/browser/context.py:911:1-929:95) method in [browser_use/browser/context.py](cci:7://file:///d:/Github/browser-use/browser_use/browser/context.py:0:0-0:0) to:
  - Add proper element state verification before input
  - Support different input field types (standard inputs and contenteditable)
  - Implement fallback mechanisms when primary input method fails
  - Add input verification to ensure text was successfully entered
  - Improve error handling with specific error messages
  - Add debug logging for better troubleshooting

## Problem Being Solved
The original implementation had several issues:
1. Text input would not be accepted despite cursor being visible
2. No proper handling of different input field types
3. Operator crashes when using the pause button
4. Lack of proper error handling and state management

## Solution Details
The solution implements a more robust text input handling system:
1. Checks element state before attempting input
2. Uses appropriate input method based on element type:
   - `fill()` for standard input fields
   - `evaluate()` + `type()` for contenteditable elements
   - Fallback to `press_sequentially()` if primary method fails
3. Verifies input success (except for password fields)
4. Adds proper timeouts and state management
5. Uses project's `BrowserError` class for consistent error handling

## Testing Done
- Tested with standard input fields
- Tested with contenteditable elements
- Verified error handling with invalid elements
- Checked input verification functionality
- Tested network state handling

## Breaking Changes
None. This is a backward-compatible improvement to existing functionality.

## Additional Notes
- Added debug logging to help with future troubleshooting
- Maintained consistent code style with the project (using tabs)
- Used existing project patterns and error handling mechanisms

## Related Issues
Fixes #543

## Checklist
- [x] Code follows project style guidelines
- [x] Added appropriate error handling
- [x] Added debug logging
- [x] Maintained backward compatibility
- [x] Tested with different input types
- [x] Documentation updated (docstring)

title: Fix documentation: Correct default value of planner_interval from 4 to 1
body:
The documentation incorrectly states that the default value of `planner_interval` is **4**, whereas the actual default value in the code is **1**.

#### **Issue**
In the documentation:
> `planner_interval: Number of steps between planning phases. Defaults to 4.`

However, in the `Agent` class constructor, the default value is explicitly set to `1`:

https://github.com/browser-use/browser-use/blob/471ecb1009228b0d4280dd1b3952e8937f437a32/browser_use/agent/service.py#L107

#### **Fix**
Updated the documentation to reflect the correct default value (`1`) to match the actual implementation.

body:
### Key Improvements:
1. **Error Handling for Subprocess**:
   - Added a `try-except` block around the `subprocess.Popen` call to catch and log any errors during Chrome startup.
   - Raised a `RuntimeError` with a meaningful message if the subprocess fails to start.

2. **Retry Logic**:
   - Added a loop to retry connecting to the Chrome instance after starting it.
   - Logged each retry attempt for better debugging.

3. **Final Connection Attempt**:
   - After retries, a final attempt is made to connect to the Chrome instance. If this fails, a `RuntimeError` is raised with a clear message.

4. **Logging**:
   - Added detailed logging for each step, including retries and connection attempts, to help diagnose issues.

title: Intermediate tabs properly closed
body:
**Title:** `fix: Ensure intermediate tabs are properly closed before opening new ones`  

**Resolves:** #601  

---

### **Issue Description**  
The agent was expected to close intermediate tabs before opening new ones, but logs showed that no tabs were actually closed. This caused multiple unused tabs to remain open, potentially leading to performance issues and resource leaks.  

#### **Reproduction Steps**  
1. Run the agent with multiple tabs opening in sequence.  
2. Observe that intermediate tabs are not being closed.  
3. Expectation: The agent should close all but the last opened tab before proceeding.  
4. Actual Result: Tabs remain open despite logs indicating closures.  

---

### **Fix Details**  
- Implemented `close_intermediate_tabs` method.  
- Retrieves the current browser session and context.  
- Ensures all but the last opened tab are closed.  
- Added a safeguard to check if a tab is already closed before attempting to close it.  
- Logs successful closures and warnings on failures.  

### **Affected File**
- browser-use/browser_use/browser/context.py

Looking forward to feedback! 🚀

Additionally, it improves the calculation of the DOM elements in the JS eval script by ignoring the added indicator elements.

The test cases require this action to properly validate the model outputs. ### **Changes Made** 1. **Added `ExtractPageContentAction`** in `browser_use/controller/views.py` to support test validation. 2. **Fix missing page_summary in Agent Brain** 3. **Updated interacted elements** in `AgentHistory` samples to include meaningful interactions (`xpath` values). 4. **Updated agent tests** (`browser_use/agent/tests.py`) to include `extract_page_content` in expected outputs. 5. **Fixed assertion issues** by ensuring correct dictionary comparisons for action outputs. ### **Why This Change?** - The test suite was missing `ExtractPageContentAction`, leading to assertion errors. - Ensures the agent's model outputs align with expected behavior. - Improves test reliability by correctly handling page content extraction. ### **Impact & Risk** ✅ **Low risk** – This change only introduces an action already referenced in tests. ✅ **Backward compatible** – No existing logic is modified, only extended to support test cases. ### **Next Steps** - Merge this PR to ensure test cases pass. - Validate with other agents to check for similar missing actions. Let me know if you need any adjustments! 🚀 ### **❌Before the Changes** Even before add the `ExtractPageContentAction`, it has 8 errors occur, this pull request will fix the bugs in the test case: ### **✅ After the Changes**

title: Fix redundant <a> tag
body:
This PR resolves https://github.com/browser-use/browser-use/issues/640

The issue is that the <a> tags have a single child (the text node) but if the text node is not visible (isTextNodeVisible() returns false) the textnode is returned as null in builDomTree.js and later on when the user prompt is formed, the empty "<a><a/>" is sent to llm. This is increasing the token count and confusing the llm.

I fixed it by adding a check that if tag is <a> and child is null, then don't add the <a> to nodeData in buildDomTree.js
This change won't hamper other cases when <a> has img as child or anything else as child.


[before logs](https://drive.google.com/file/d/1yPav2S2eWmYOyLCq0jMaEFPiDaorYC7U/view?usp=drive_link)
[after logs](https://drive.google.com/file/d/1pOPZd20Uzl8UZQx0x0HI1Mxae6ay_zmU/view?usp=sharing)

title: Update Sample Code to Properly Utilize DeepSeek API Key for Dual LLM Usage
body:
I noticed that the sample code in [this commit](https://github.com/browser-use/browser-use/commit/98f159e8b4295a07aacd6bbed9a212b1fbf0ca2f#diff-30808312c8d80d554b811329fee070cd52bf72b0a3ef5c0165bd8cf547bae32a) references `DEEPSEEK_API_KEY` and uses `SecretStr`, yet these elements are not utilized in the subsequent code. The commit message suggests that the original intent was to demonstrate a sample using two different LLMs.

**Proposed Changes:**  
- Replace the current instantiation:  
  ```python
  llm = ChatOpenAI(model='gpt-4o', temperature=0.0)
  ```  
- With the following:  
  ```python
  llm = ChatOpenAI(
      base_url='https://api.deepseek.com/v1',
      model='deepseek-chat',
      api_key=SecretStr(api_key),
  )
  ```

**Rationale:**  
This update properly utilizes the DeepSeek API key and aligns the sample code with the intended demonstration of using two LLMs. It helps ensure that the example code accurately reflects the documented functionality.

This pull request introduces a new advanced search functionality in the `examples/custom-functions/advanced_search.py` file. The changes include importing necessary libraries, setting up environment variables, and defining a new asynchronous function to search the web using the Tessa API.

Key changes:

* Added necessary imports including `json`, `os`, `sys`, `requests`, `asyncio`, `dotenv`, `langchain_openai`, and `pydantic`.
* Configured the `Controller` to exclude specific actions and set up the `BEARER_TOKEN` from environment variables.
* Defined an asynchronous function `search_web` to perform a web search using the Tessa API and filter results based on a minimum score.
* Implemented a `main` function to create a task, initialize an `Agent` with a specific task and model, and run the agent asynchronously.
* Ensured the script runs the `main` function asynchronously when executed directly.

title: fix(context): reload page for CDP remote browser connections
body:
Problem
When using CDP (Chrome DevTools Protocol) connections, page operations were resulting in timeout errors after 30000ms. This specifically occurred during page load state verification: await page.wait_for_load_state()
The error manifests in the following call stack:

context.py line 219 - Initial wait_for_load_state call Propagates through Playwright's async API
Times out in frame implementation while waiting for load state

Solution
Implemented page reloading specifically for CDP connections to prevent these timeout errors. This addresses the underlying issue where the page load state was not being properly detected in CDP scenarios. 

Implementation Details

Added conditional page reload for CDP connection types Maintains existing behavior for non-CDP connections Ensures proper page load state verification

Testing

Verified fix resolves timeout errors with CDP connections Confirmed existing functionality remains intact for other connection types

Reference
Solution approach based on discord support ticket - https://discord.com/channels/1303749220842340412/1334218695509016657/1334517519611990056

title: enhance isInteractiveElement to recognize dropdown containers as inte…
body:
This commit resolves an issue where the `isInteractiveElement` function failed to flag dropdown container elements as interactive. The function now recursively checks child elements for interactivity and considers the container interactive if any child meets the criteria.

Added support for specific dropdown-related attributes such as `data-action="a-dropdown-select"` and roles like `combobox` or `dropdown`. This ensures better detection of interactive dropdown components.

Changes include:
- Recursive check for child elements' interactivity.
- Explicit handling of dropdown-related attributes and roles.
- Edge case handling to avoid false positives for `body` and its direct children.

Fixes the bug where dropdowns were not recognized as interactive unless debug overrides were used.

Reproduction steps:
1. Run the `buildDomTree` function with dropdown components in the DOM.
2. Confirm that dropdown containers are now flagged as interactive without modifying the function manually.

title: Made click element action more robust
body:
Issue link: https://github.com/browser-use/browser-use/issues/629
The issue primarily occurred because the click element didn't acknowledge that the page navigated and it still continued to click on the existing element. Also, the code was not waiting for the page to be loaded completely. Also, it didn't have proper retry mechanism. So, without retry, it was just calling the llm again and again with below errors, which in turn was increasing token count as well.

These were the warnings and errors:
`WARNING  [controller] Element not clickable with index 12 - most likely the page changed`
`Error: Failed to click element: Page.evaluate: Execution context was destroyed, most likely because of a navigation`

So, these are the changes I did:
- created a new ElementClickHandler class to shift the click handling logic there.
- added code to handle retry (default is 3 tries).
- added code to handle popups.
- added code to handle navigation.
- all the timeouts and retries are configurable.

This is the prompt i used to test the code (I improved the prompt given by the user in corresponding issue):
[prompt](https://drive.google.com/file/d/19uiI8uJpdcJ5VfmebOtk8_ZIAfrS-dyn/view?usp=sharing)

These are additional file for reference:
[logs](https://drive.google.com/file/d/1I6NKlMzMdPeVA7ICgRQ9UYcITIl5IUcT/view?usp=sharing)
[gif](https://drive.google.com/file/d/1SUzT6jRmoG99V-QwGNRrIDcLxtDK-FjI/view?usp=sharing)

way forward:
the ElementClickHandler can be further improved to handle unnecessary overlays (other than popups) which sometimes cover the clickable elements and hamper the clicking functionality. This can be put in roadmap.

title: Fix Schema Validation for AgentOutput
body:
# Description

This PR addresses the schema validation issue for the `AgentOutput` class in the `agent/views.py` file. The previous implementation allowed an empty array for the `action` field, which caused errors in function calls. This update ensures that the `action` field is properly defined, requiring at least one action to be specified.

---

## Changes Made

### Updated `AgentOutput` Class
- Defined the `action` field with proper metadata using Pydantic's `Field`.
- Set `min_items=1` to enforce that at least one action is provided.
- Added a description to clarify the purpose of the field.

```python
class AgentOutput(BaseModel):
    ...
    action: list[ActionModel] = Field(
        ...,  # This means the field is required
        description="List of actions to execute",
        min_items=1,  # Ensure at least one action is provided
    )
```

### Modified `type_with_custom_actions` Method
- Ensured that the new `action` field schema is preserved when creating dynamic models.

```python
@staticmethod
def type_with_custom_actions(custom_actions: Type[ActionModel]) -> Type['AgentOutput']:
    ...
    action=(
        list[custom_actions],
        Field(
            ...,
            description="List of actions to execute",
            min_items=1
        )
    ),
```

---

## Testing
- The changes have been tested against the existing functionality to ensure compatibility.
- Additional tests can be added to verify the behavior of the `AgentOutput` class with various action inputs.

---

## Related Issues
- Resolves #759 (Invalid schema for function 'AgentOutput')

The error occurs during the execution of the action function from the production code (Registry.execute_action), not because the test is written incorrectly. In the failing call for the action “test_action_with_browser”, the action function requires a “browser” parameter. Even though the test passes “browser=mock_browser” in one call, when testing the error case (i.e. calling the action without providing a browser), the production code directly calls the function without any pre-check. As a consequence, Python raises a TypeError for the missing required argument “browser”. The exception is then caught and re-raised as a RuntimeError with an unexpected message. This behavior indicates a bug in the production code: it does not properly detect or handle the missing “browser” argument in a user-friendly way (or with the expected error message), causing the test to fail.
- `browser_use/agent/service.py`
  > 
The error occurs because when the registry’s execute_action function is called (with extra keyword arguments such as browser=mock_browser), the registered action function isn’t receiving the extra “browser” argument. In the test, the async function test_action_with_browser expects two arguments (param1 and browser), but it is invoked with only “param1” due to a bug in the code under test (or its mocking/wrapping in the registry) that fails to merge or forward the extra arguments properly. title: Added extension support in playwright built in browser
body:
Issue link: https://github.com/browser-use/browser-use/issues/727

The task was to add adblocker in the playwright instance. I thought of using Ublock Origin, but Chrome is soon deprecating it because it doesn't follow Manifest V3. So, I added Ublock Lite.
If the flag enable_adblock is True, the chrome extension will be downloaded from official github release only during first run. We will not re-download the extension again and again, instead we will reuse the previously download one after the first run.

I tried using normal context of playwright, but I found out that extensions require persistent context. So that is why the code of creating persistent context is in context.py.

These are the [logs](https://drive.google.com/file/d/1m2lfo8JkI9_WObOuRuaSK6g0M7iWGkGY/view?usp=sharing).

No existing tests required updates.
## 🐛 Bug Detection
Potential issues found in the following files:
- `browser_use/browser/context.py`
  > The failure occurs in the test_reset_context where the test expects that both DummyPage instances (page1 and page2) have their "closed" attribute set to True. In the implementation of reset_context, the code iterates directly over session.context.pages and for each page calls await page.close(). In our DummyPage implementation the close() method removes the page from the context’s pages list. This removal mutates the list in-place during iteration, causing one of the pages to be skipped. Because of this, one page (in this case, page2) is never processed by the loop and remains unclosed, leading to the failing assertion.
This indicates that the bug lies in the BrowserContext.reset_context method in the production code. To fix it, the code should iterate over a copy of the list (e.g., using list(session.context.pages)) so that removal during the loop does not cause items to be skipped.
Thus, this error is caused by the code being tested (a bug in reset_context), not by the test itself or its settings.
- `browser_use/controller/service.py`
  > There are two failing tests, and each failure points to a problem in the implementation rather than a problem of how the tests are written or simply in the test configuration.
1. In TestAgent.test_step_error_handling the test asserts that the Agent instance should have an attribute called consecutive_failures (set to 1 after an error). However, the Agent class does not have any such attribute defined. The test is expecting error‐handling behavior (incrementing a “failure counter”) that is not implemented in the Agent code. In other words, the error is caused by a missing property (or an omission in the error handling routine) in the Agent implementation.
2. In TestRegistry.test_execute_action_with_and_without_browser_context the error comes from executing an action function that requires a “browser” argument (it is defined as async def test_action_with_browser(param1: str, browser)) but the extra keyword arguments passed from execute_action are not being forwarded properly. As a result, when execute_action calls the side_effect function, it does not supply the required “browser” argument even when one is provided in the extra arguments; this mismatch in the signature is causing the missing argument error. This indicates a bug in the handling of extra arguments (and possibly in the way the function signature is interpreted) in the Registry.execute_action implementation.
Both of these issues are problems in the code under test (Agent and Registry) rather than shortcomings in how the tests or test settings are written.
Therefore, the failures are due to bugs in the code.

title: Fix/agent history max steps #439
body:
# **Fix: Store "Failed to complete task in max steps" in Agent History**  #439 

## **Overview**  
This update ensures that when the agent **fails due to exceeding max steps**, the error is properly **stored in history** instead of just being logged.  

## **Changes Made**  
### **Before (Issue)**  
```python
else:
    logger.info('❌ Failed to complete task in maximum steps')
```
🔴 **Issue**: The error was not recorded in `self.state.history.history`, leaving history empty.  

### **After (Fix)**  
```python
else:
    error_message = 'Failed to complete task in maximum steps'
    
    self.state.history.history.append(
        AgentHistory(
            model_output=None,
            result=[ActionResult(error=error_message, include_in_memory=True)],
            state=BrowserStateHistory(url="", title="", tabs=[], interacted_element=[], screenshot=None),
            metadata=None
        )
    )

    logger.info(f'❌ {error_message}')
```
✅ **Fix**:  
- Stores error in **Agent History List**.  
- Prevents history from being **empty on failure**.

body:
sometimes a click happens but the page fails to load in time, in this line,
```
await page.wait_for_load_state()
```

Then the except will try to click on a non-existing element and fail anyways. This change makes sure that we retry the click only when the click fails.

It will not save all use-cases, if the element was actually clicked and the page has changed the `eval` will still fail with
```
Error('Page.evaluate: Execution context was destroyed, most likely because of a navigation')
```

Another option would be to add some configurations to the timeout and not have it static 1500ms

title: Efficient Detection of Interactive Elements using computed cursor style
body:
## Background
In most web applications, developers or frameworks provide visual cues to indicate interactive elements. One common approach is changing the cursor style when hovering over such elements. This helps users quickly identify elements they can interact with.

Upon analyzing widely used websites such as Amazon, Google, eBay, Salesforce, Reddit, Google Docs  etc., I observed a consistent pattern: interactive elements typically have cursor styles that differ from the default pointer, signaling interactivity.

## Implementation
To enhance this behavior, I have implemented the doesElementHaveInteractivePointer function. This function determines whether an element has an interactive cursor by inspecting its computed cursor style via window.getComputedStyle().

Key advantages of this approach:

- Performance Optimization: It eliminates the need for more expensive DOM traversal operations (e.g., closest()) and avoids calls to window.getEventListeners().
- Efficiency: By directly checking the computed styles, it removes the need to create additional data structures such as sets, improving execution speed.
- Additionally removed the unused call to window.getComputedStyle() in the same function.

This implementation ensures a lightweight and efficient way to detect interactive elements, aligning with best practices in web development.

body:
The program only has separate support for deepseek-reasoner, but I found that for some models, such as deepseek-chat, which does not support tool_call, the program did not convert the input.
My code incorporates a conversion retry after an error is reported to ensure that the entire code does not fail because the user message in the tool_call is not in context.
There are a few issues, including  #1020, that report getting stuck in blank pages and stuck in step1 indefinitely, because our browser-use default installed dependency package does not include google, and the error is not caught properly. To fix this, add google to the dependency package. But the root cause is that users are using an unsupported model.

This pr helps some users solve the problem by adapting the model to solve the error.
程序只对deepseek-reasoner进行了单独的支持，但是我发现对于一些模型，比如deepseek-chat等不支持tool_call的模型，程序没有对输入做转换。
我的代码加入了报错后的转换重试，确保代码不会因为用户消息在tool_call不在context中而导致整个代码失败。
目前有一些issue，包括#1020 这类issue，他们都反馈说会卡在blank页面并无限卡在step1，这是因为我们的browser-use默认安装的依赖包不包括google，错误没有被正常捕获而导致的。要修复这个问题应将google加入到依赖包中。但根本原因是因为用户使用了不受支持的模型。

`(WIP) pending confirmation that this is useful/needed`

My code in this PR fixes the immediate issue of not being able to detect the most recently opened foreground tab properly, but the long-term fix is to refactor the code to better track which tab is "current" for the agent vs "current" for the human watching. Keeping those separate would allow a user to continue using their browser normally without breaking `browser-use`'s interactions with a particular tab.

If it's not a design goal of `browser-use` to allow parallel browser driving by agent & human on separate tabs, let me know and I will change my approach.

title: Ensure viewPortExpansion properly filters elements outside the viewport
body:
### **Fix: Ensure `viewPortExpansion` properly filters elements outside the viewport**  

Fixes https://github.com/browser-use/browser-use/issues/1247

#### **Description**  
While working with browser interactions, I noticed that the `viewPortExpansion` parameter had no effect on filtering elements in the `SelectorMap`. As a result, elements outside the viewport were still selectable by the LLM, even when `viewport_expansion = 0`.  

This issue was caused by the fact that `isInExpandedViewport` was **defined but never actually used**. The previous implementation contained an inline viewport check, but it did not consistently exclude elements that were outside the visible area on scrollable pages.  

#### **Fix**  
- The existing function `isInExpandedViewport` is now used to filter out elements properly.  
- This ensures that only elements within the expanded viewport are included in the `SelectorMap`.  
- The behavior now correctly respects `viewport_expansion` values, preventing unintended selections.  

#### **Impact**  
- Fixes incorrect element selection on scrollable pages.  
- Ensures that `viewport_expansion` behaves as expected.  
- Reduces unnecessary processing of off-screen elements.  

Let me know if any further refinements are needed! 🚀

title: Implement LLM+P planning approach with vector DB integration
body:
/Fixed #778
/claim #778 


# Planning by using only LLMs is not working well. It generates extra information (hallucination) and often fails to produce optimal plans for complex tasks.


This PR implements a hybrid planning approach that combines:
LLM+P: Integration of classical planning with LLM-based planning
Vector DB: Storage and retrieval of successful past plans for context enhancement
Key Components
1. Classical Planning Integration (LLM+P)
Implemented PDDL conversion for browser automation tasks
Integrated pyperplan for optimal plan generation
Added translation from PDDL plans back to natural language instructions
2. Vector Database for Plan Retrieval
Added FAISS vector store to save successful plans
Implemented similarity search to find relevant past examples
Created plan refinement using successful examples as context
3. Robust Error Handling
Added comprehensive error handling to gracefully degrade when components fail
Ensured planning continues even if classical planning or vector DB fails
Implementation Details
New Dependencies:
```
pyperplan==2.1.0
langchain-openai>=0.0.2
langchain-community>=0.0.16

```
Key Methods
_refine_with_classical_planner: Converts plans to PDDL and uses pyperplan
_enhance_with_vector_db: Retrieves similar plans from vector DB
_refine_next_steps_with_examples: Uses past examples to improve current plan
Testing
All tests are passing. The implementation has been tested with:
Running Tests:

```
# Install dependencies
pip install pyperplan==2.1.0 langchain-openai>=0.0.2 langchain-community>=0.0.16

# Run the tests
pytest browser_use/agent/tests.py -v

```
Test Cases
test_last_action: Verifies the last action is correctly retrieved
test_all_model_actions: Ensures all model actions are properly tracked
Planning integration tests with mock browser state
Usage Example
The planning service is automatically used by the agent at configurable intervals:

```
# Create planning service with default 5-step interval
planning_service = PlanningService(
    message_manager=message_manager,
    agent_llm=agent_llm,
    planner_interval=5  # Plan every 5 steps
)

# Planning is triggered automatically during agent execution
# or can be manually triggered:
plan = await planning_service.plan_next_steps(step_info, browser_state)

```



Configuration Options
The planning service can be configured with:
planner_interval: How often to run planning (default: every 5 steps)
use_vision_for_planner: Whether to include screenshots in planning (default: True)
planner_llm: Optional separate LLM for planning (defaults to agent's LLM)
Benefits
1. Reduced Hallucination: Classical planning ensures logical consistency
Improved Plan Quality: Optimal plans from classical planning algorithms
Learning from Experience: Vector DB enables learning from past successful tasks
Graceful Degradation: System falls back to LLM-only planning when needed
Future Work
Integration with specialized models fine-tuned for browser tasks
Expanding the PDDL domain to cover more browser automation scenarios
Implementing more sophisticated plan merging strategies

Overview
This PR adds anti-fingerprinting capabilities to the browser-use library to help avoid bot detection mechanisms like those used by Cloudflare and DataDome. Changes
Added anti_fingerprint flag to BrowserConfig (default: False)
Implemented methods to load and apply anti-fingerprinting scripts
Created scripts that:
Override navigator properties to hide automation indicators
Create realistic browser plugins and mime types
Modify WebGL parameters to mimic a real device
Add subtle noise to canvas operations to prevent canvas fingerprinting
Add subtle noise to audio operations to prevent audio fingerprinting
Ensured patches are applied to all pages in a context
Added event listener to apply patches to new pages
Usage
Users can enable anti-fingerprinting by setting anti_fingerprint=True in their BrowserConfig:

```
browser = Browser(
    config=BrowserConfig(
        headless=False,
        anti_fingerprint=True
    )
)

Unit tests for message hashing
Unit tests for cache entry expiration
Unit tests for cache settings and strategies
To run the tests:

```
pytest tests/test_cache.py -v

```
Performance Impact
This caching system should significantly improve performance for repeated tasks:
First run: Normal execution time (cache miss)
Subsequent runs: Faster execution time (cache hit)
The cache uses file-based storage with configurable TTL (Time-To-Live) settings to ensure data freshness.
Usage
The caching system can be used by passing cache_settings to the create_agent_with_cache method:

```
agent = await browser.create_agent_with_cache(
    task="Search for information about Python",
    llm=llm,
    controller=controller,
    cache_settings=CacheSettings(
        strategy=CacheStrategy.READ_WRITE,
        ttl_seconds=3600,
        max_entries=100,
        cache_llm_responses=True,
        cache_agent_runs=True
    )
)

```
Future Improvements
Add more comprehensive tests for complex caching scenarios
Implement cache invalidation strategies
Add support for distributed caching (e.g., Redis)
Improve cache hit rate metrics and monitoring

title: Open cross-origin iframes in a new tab to avoid needing `--disable-web-security`
body:
Related issues (this first-pass PR does not fully fix all of these, but it should help):

- https://github.com/browser-use/browser-use/issues/700 (azure nested iframes)
- https://github.com/browser-use/browser-use/issues/853 (salesforce nested iframes)
- https://github.com/browser-use/browser-use/issues/566 (amazon iframes)
- https://github.com/browser-use/browser-use/issues/923 (captcha.com demo iframes)
- https://github.com/browser-use/browser-use/issues/443 (some other payment gateway iframe)

---

This PR attempts to break CORS from the agent's perspectve and allow `buildDOMTree.js` to traverse cross-origin iframes just like it currently does non-cross-origin iframes. Unfortunately the same approach used for same-origin frames is not possible, browser security forces us to go around the wall via playwright instead, but this introduces several new hurdles.

We have to create a new id translation mapping that mutates all the subframe generated DOM trees to reconnect the references to cross-origin parents & children. We also have to deterministically merge/offset all the IDs and update child id references to prevent conflicts, without introducing any dependency between frames during tree generation to keep it parallel.

---

#### The main challenges

- playwright doesn't deterministically provide all the frames in the first place‼️ with identical settings some pageloads `page.frames` contain cross-origin frames, exit, retry and the next time it doesn't, retry a few times then it does, etc. there is a race or timing issue
- iframes arent guaranteed to have any id, name, or unique src url, the standard API to pierce and find a nested iframe [only accepts `name=` or `url=`](https://github.com/microsoft/playwright/issues/7982) as lookup params and nothing else.
- iframes and their content can be added/removed/updated multiple times per second by JS, and their context handles and all child handles (and potentially nested frames) break any time they navigate
- non-cross-origin iframes can nested inside cross-origin iframes and vice versa up to 3x deep
 	
#### In an ideal world we'd want

- every `<iframe />` to have a stable and globally unique `name="..."` or `url="..."` attr
- which means `page.frame('name')` works to pierce and get that specific iframe even if nested
- it also lets us merge separate DOMTree maps without conflicts because every frame ends up with a unique xpath `/html/body/iframe[somename]/html/body/iframe[othername]`
- all frames should inject `buildDOMTree.js` in parallel for speed, and output should be merged at the end. building it frame by frame and passing the growing `indexOffset` counter between them serially is too slow

---

#### Approaches tried

- [x] ~~pre-tagging every iframe encountered with a `data-browser-use-iframe-id={idx}` attr~~ doesn't work because JS frameworks like react/vue/etc redraw the element immediately, also doesn't solve the issue of how to pierce parent frames to find the element later
- [x] ~~using playwright to trick the browser into thinking it's a same-origin domain by rewriting the iframe request and response URLs~~ too complex/browser security prevents it without crazy root CA hacks
- [x] ~~passing an `indexOffset` counter into `buildDOMTree.js` so the IDs it generates don't conflict with the parent frame~~ forces them to run serially, or forces us to switch to a longer ID format w/ random ids (which might break vision, the system prompt, or lower LLM success)
- [x] ~~give up on nested and non-unique iframes and only support top-level cross-origin and same-origin iframes~~ I got this 1/2 working but it's slow and makes some pages more buggy
- [x] ⭐️ **SIMPLEST SOLUTION: if any visible (non-ads) cross-origin iframe is present on the page, simply open the url for it in a new tab and treat it like a separate page, with a special title telling the LLM it's a popup that should be treated as part of the previous page**

title: fix: Move HTTPX client cleanup from agent to browser close
body:
The original original PR ([#895](https://github.com/browser-use/browser-use/pull/895)) addressed the resource warnings and potential memory leaks by adding HTTPX client cleanup to the agent's closing procedure, it introduced a new issue in multi-agent scenarios.  
When one agent closes, it cleans up ALL HTTPX clients in memory, including those being used by other agents in the same context.  

### Reference Demo
test.py
```  python
import os
import sys
import asyncio

sys.path.append(os.path.dirname(os.path.dirname(os.path.abspath(__file__))))

from langchain_openai import ChatOpenAI
from dotenv import load_dotenv

from browser_use import Agent, Browser

# Load environment variables
load_dotenv()
if not os.getenv('OPENAI_API_KEY'):
    raise ValueError('OPENAI_API_KEY is not set. Please add it to your environment variables.')

async def main():
    browser = Browser()
    async with await browser.new_context() as context:
        model = ChatOpenAI(model='gpt-4o')

        # Initialize browser agent
        agent1 = Agent(
            task='search iphone 17 news on google and pick 3 sources.',
            llm=model,
            browser_context=context,
        )
        agent2 = Agent(
            task='compare all the content found and summarize the key information about iPhone 17.',
            llm=model,
            browser_context=context,
        )
        await agent1.run()
        await agent2.run()

if __name__ == "__main__":
    asyncio.run(main())
```  

### Fix
This PR moves HTTPX cleanup from agent to browser level to:
- Avoid breaking the multi-agent tasks, only cleans connections when browser fully closes.  
- Respects the _force_keep_browser_alive flag.

## Background

- In web applications, `<label>` elements are often used to enhance accessibility and usability by moving focus to or toggling elements like checkboxes and radio buttons.  
- A `<label>` with a non-empty `for` attribute is considered interactive since it associates the label with another form control.  
- Some users have reported issues with detecting checkboxes due to improper label handling. This PR improves the detection mechanism and addresses #871.

## Implementation

This PR introduces the `isInteractiveLabel` function to improve label detection by:  
- Ensuring the element is a `<label>` tag.  
- Verifying that the `for` attribute is non-empty.  
- Checking if the `for` attribute references a valid interactive element (`<input>`, `<textarea>`, `<select>`, or `<button>`).  

By implementing this function, we enhance the ability to detect interactive labels and improve overall user interaction.

title: Add support for procedural memory for running agents for longer tasks using mem0
body:
# Add Procedural Memory Support Using Mem0

This PR adds support for procedural memory in browser-use using [Mem0](https://mem0.ai), which helps agents run longer tasks more reliably while using fewer tokens.

## What's Changed

- Added a Memory service that generates procedural memories at configurable intervals
- Integrated memory generation into the agent's step cycle
- Added memory configuration options to the Agent constructor
- Implemented conditions to generate memory only when enabled and at specified intervals

## Configuration Options

Memory can be configured through these parameters when initializing an Agent:

```python
# Memory settings
enable_memory: bool = True             # Enable/disable memory feature
memory_interval: int = 10              # Generate memory every N steps
memory_config: Optional[dict] = None   # Additional Mem0-specific configuration
```

## Benefits

- **Token Efficiency**: By summarizing past steps into procedural memory, we reduce the token count in the agent's context
- **Improved Reliability**: Agents can better remember previous actions and their outcomes over longer tasks
- **Configurable Usage**: Memory generation is fully configurable and can be disabled if not needed

## Results

Ran for a long task for visiting 50 links and summarizing the content for all the links. Here are the results:

## Overview
This PR adds support for using persistent browser sessions via user data directories. This enables users to maintain browser state (cookies, localStorage, sessions) across multiple instances/runs of their browser automation scripts.

## Key Changes
- Added `user_data_dir` and `profile_directory` parameters to the `BrowserConfig` class
- Implemented support for Playwright's `launch_persistent_context` method 
- Added handling for persistent contexts in the browser session management
- Adjusted error handling and logging for persistent context scenarios
- Added comprehensive documentation and examples

## Implementation Details
- When a `user_data_dir` is specified, we use Playwright's method for creating a persistent context
- This persistent context is stored in a new `_persistent_context` field in the `Browser` class
- Chrome/Chromium profiles can be specified using the `profile_directory` parameter
- The implementation preserves existing behavior when no user data directory is specified

## Testing
The implementation has been tested with:
- Basic persistence of cookies and localStorage values
- Profile directory usage with Chrome/Chromium
- Error handling for invalid directories
- Ensuring proper cleanup on session close

## Documentation
Added detailed documentation in `docs/browser/user_data_dir.md` covering:
- Overview and purpose of the feature
- Configuration options
- Browser compatibility notes 
- Example usage
- Common use cases

## Example Scripts
Added example scripts demonstrating:
1. Basic user data directory usage
2. Working with Chrome/Chromium profiles

## Future Considerations
- Enhanced profile management capabilities
- Better handling of browser shutdown issues
- Additional options for privacy/security settings when using persistent sessions

## Breaking Changes
None. This implementation is fully backward compatible with existing code.

Issue link: https://github.com/browser-use/browser-use/issues/1207
### Root cause:
In this code, the `await browser.switch_to_tab(params.page_id)` perfectly switches to the desired tab but the next line `page = await browser.get_current_page()` is switching to the last tab because it internally calls `return non_extension_pages[-1]`:
```
@self.registry.action('Switch tab', param_model=SwitchTabAction)
		async def switch_tab(params: SwitchTabAction, browser: BrowserContext):
			await browser.switch_to_tab(params.page_id)
			# Wait for tab to be ready
			page = await browser.get_current_page()
			await page.wait_for_load_state()
			msg = f'🔄  Switched to tab {params.page_id}'
			logger.info(msg)
			return ActionResult(extracted_content=msg, include_in_memory=True)
```

### Fix:
I have fixed it by adding active_tab class member field. I have added it in all those methods that are responsible for opening/closing a tab.

The `system_prompt_class` parameter has been removed and replaced with two new parameters: `override_system_message` and `extend_system_message`. The new parameters offer two ways to customize the system prompt:
- `override_system_message`: Completely replace the default system prompt with a custom one
- `extend_system_message`: Add additional instructions to the default system prompt

This change simplifies the system prompt customization process and makes it more intuitive for users. The documentation has been updated to reflect these changes.

title: added episodic memory actions
body:
The current implementation of browser-use doesn't have memory. Although recently procedural memory was added [here](https://github.com/browser-use/browser-use/pull/1205), it is different from episodic memory.
Procedural memory is use for storing summaries of steps like (what to do and how to do). [here](https://github.com/mem0ai/mem0/blob/main/mem0/configs/prompts.py#L211-L288) is the mem0  prompt for procedural memory.
Episodic memory is used to store some facts. We need this. Some people have reported that if they run tasks which have like 100+ steps, then the browser-use agent gets stuck somewhere and loops over the same step again and again. for eg, if we prompt it to do research about some 100 items, it will loop again and again over one item even though it has processed it successfully. I think this can be solved if we allow the agent to memorize some data locally. Currently we are using the [system prompt](https://github.com/browser-use/browser-use/blob/main/browser_use/agent/prompts.py#L107) to tell the llm to memorize everything, but that is not turning out to be successful.

In this PR, I have implemented some actions to save, retreive, delete data in the memory store (faiss vector store). I have taken inspration from AgentZero. AgentZero also exposes some tool/actions to the llm like [MemorySave](https://github.com/frdel/agent-zero/blob/main/python/tools/memory_save.py). It uses faiss as a store.

I thought of using faiss directly but I thought mem0 will provide better optimisations and good abstraction. Also, we have already integrated mem0 for procedural memory. That is why this PR uses mem0.

WIP: I am getting some issue in running the embedding model with gemini (getting assertion error). I have asked this on mem0 [github](https://github.com/mem0ai/mem0/issues/2430#issuecomment-2780714084) too. When this is tested, I'll open this PR for review.

Meanwhile I want that this PR gets reviewed. If there is some other approach, we can use that as well. @deshraj  if you could give some insights, it would be really helpful.

title: Fix incorrect documentation for SystemPrompt customization
body:
### Summary
This PR fixes incorrect information in the official documentation ([link](https://docs.browser-use.com/customize/system-prompt)) related to customizing SystemPrompt in the stable version (v0.1.40) of browser-use.

### Problem
The documentation currently suggests overriding important_rules() method, which does not exist or get called in the stable version. In v0.1.40, the only relevant method that affects the system prompt is get_system_message().

As a result, users following the documentation for the stable release will see no effect from their changes, leading to confusion and potential misimplementation.

### What’s Changed
Updated the example code to override the correct method get_system_message() instead of the non-functional important_rules() method. Also included how to properly append custom rules to the existing system prompt using prompt_template.

### Suggested Fix in Docs (Before → After)
#### Before:
```python
from browser_use import Agent, SystemPrompt

class MySystemPrompt(SystemPrompt):
    def important_rules(self) -> str:
        # Get existing rules from parent class
        existing_rules = super().important_rules()

        # Add your custom rules
        new_rules = """
9. MOST IMPORTANT RULE:
- ALWAYS open first a new tab and go to wikipedia.com no matter the task!!!
"""

        # Make sure to use this pattern otherwise the exiting rules will be lost
        return f'{existing_rules}\n{new_rules}'
```

#### After:
```python
from browser_use import SystemPrompt
from langchain_core.messages import SystemMessage
from overrides import overrides
class MySystemPrompt(SystemPrompt):
    @overrides
    def get_system_message(self) -> SystemMessage:
        
        # Get existing rules from parent class
        existing_prompt = self.prompt_template.format(max_actions=self.max_actions_per_step)

        # Add your custom rules
        new_prompt = """
            10. MOST IMPORTANT RULE:
            - You must response, think, reason Only Korean
            - You must find "ReactModal__Overlay" attribute when you search sections
            - You must search another apporach, another section, another actions even you faced retry the situations over twice times
        """

        # Make sure to use this pattern otherwise the exiting rules will be lost
        return SystemMessage(content=f'{existing_prompt}\n{new_prompt}')
```
### Why It Matters
This correction helps new users get started without confusion and ensures the documentation aligns with the currently shipped stable version.

### Notes
I understand this was fixed in the beta version, but most users are on the stable version, and documentation should not mislead them.

Suggest clearly indicating version compatibility or updating the stable docs accordingly.

### According issues
close #1298

title: fix: fix BrowserContext initialization in new_context method
body:
### Problem  
When `config=None` is passed to `Browser.new_context()`, it passes the BrowserConfig object directly to BrowserContext rather than allowing `BrowserContext.__init__` to handle the config creation logic properly.
```  
def __init__(
  self,
  browser: 'Browser',
  config: BrowserContextConfig | None = None,
  state: Optional[BrowserContextState] = None,
):
  self.context_id = str(uuid.uuid4())
  
  self.config = config or BrowserContextConfig(**(browser.config.model_dump() if browser.config else {}))
```  

resulting in errors like:
```  
'BrowserConfig' object has no attribute 'user_agent'
```  

![image](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/1699f052-fad2-4104-9fff-7b063b61f0fa)  

### Testing
```python  
import os
import sys
import asyncio

from dotenv import load_dotenv
from langchain_openai import ChatOpenAI
from browser_use.browser.browser import Browser, BrowserConfig, BrowserContext
from browser_use import Agent

load_dotenv()

llm = ChatOpenAI(
	model='gpt-4o-mini',
)
task = 'Find the founders of browser-use and draft them a short personalized message'

async def main():
  browser = Browser(
    config=BrowserConfig(
      headless=False,
    )
  )
  async with await browser.new_context() as context:
    agent = Agent(
      task=task, 
      llm=llm, 
      browser_context=context,
      generate_gif=False,
      enable_memory=False,
    )
    await agent.run()

  await browser.close()

if __name__ == '__main__':
	asyncio.run(main())

```

title: feat: Add functionality to download and save images from URLs
body:
## Fix Image Download Functionality

Fixes #1258
Fixes #1328

### Problem
The agent was extracting image URLs from webpages but had no ability to save them locally when there were no download buttons to click. The agent would incorrectly report successful image downloading without actually saving any files.

### Solution
Added a new `download_images` action in `controller/service.py` that:
- Takes a list of image URLs and an optional save path as input
- Downloads images asynchronously using aiohttp
- Creates the save directory if it doesn't exist
- Generates unique filenames based on the image URL and timestamp
- Provides detailed feedback for each download (success or failure)

I have confirmed that the agent can now handle instructions like "save all the post images by making a folder called browserImages in the current directory" by properly parsing the intent and creating the requested directory.

### Testing
Tested with a task to download wallpapers on various website like reddit and others. The agent successfully downloaded images as shown in the logs:
![image](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/c43b3a55-404a-425f-9163-eda3c7fce096)
![image](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/61fdf1ea-01c2-4bb3-b648-0db81e700ca2)

### Video Demo

https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/d72c7b84-8d1e-4bb6-bd17-59870bfe9c5b


### Features
- **Path handling**: If no path is specified, saves to current directory. If a path is provided, creates that directory and saves there.
- **Concurrent downloads**: Uses asyncio to download multiple images simultaneously
- **Error handling**: Handles errors for individual images without failing the entire batch
- **Filename generation**: Creates unique, sanitized filenames based on URLs

title: Ensure element handle is visible before trying to scroll into view
body:
## What
Added a `not is_hidden` check before every `scroll_into_view_if_needed()` call.

## Why
Noticed when trying to upload a file on this [website](https://v0-download-and-upload-text.vercel.app/) the agent timed out: `Failed to locate element: ElementHandle.scroll_into_view_if_needed: Timeout 30000ms exceeded.`

When looking closer at the HTML code of the website I noticed the button for uploading itself did not have any input for `type=file`, instead it had a sibling `<input type="file" accept=".txt" class="hidden">` which was hidden. This is the element we would have needed to perform the upload.

So whenever we tried to find the element using `await browser.get_locate_element(file_upload_dom_el)`, it tried to scroll into view, but couldn't since the element was hidden.

## Testing
Tested locally with the same file upload website.

body:
<!-- This is an auto-generated description by mrge. -->
## Summary by mrge
Added Playwright locator generation for interacted elements with language selection options. This feature helps users create reliable Playwright test scripts by automatically generating locators in JavaScript or Python.

**New Features**
- Added `playwright_locator_language` agent setting that accepts `"javascript"` or `"python"` values
- Implemented automatic generation of Playwright locators for elements with XPaths
- Added locator strings to state history for each interacted element
- Updated documentation with usage instructions and requirements

**Refactors**
- Restructured element interaction tracking to support locator generation
- Improved error handling for locator generation failures

<!-- End of auto-generated description by mrge. -->

# Preface

Hello! We had a project requirement to generate Playwright locators which required changes to browser-use, so I figured I'd create a PR here to see if it made sense to include. I will say, that the, as far as I can tell, full implementation of this feature is outside the scope of browser-use, because `playwright` must be made accessible in the browser, which, by default, it is not, and seems outside the scope of browser-use.

One method of injecting `playwright` is to launch a browser with CDP enabled, run some Playwright code, "pause" the page (which opens a codegen window), and connect to that browser with browser-use over CDP. You can read more here: https://playwright.dev/python/docs/codegen#record-using-custom-setup

# Summary

This change adds a new agent setting, `playwright_locator_language` which can be set to enable Playwright locator codegen for all interacted elements. It defaults to `None`, but accepts values of `"javascript"` and `"python"`, which control the language the codegen outputs.

The generated locator string will exist in the state history as part of the agent history item.

### Example

Element with XPath `html/body/dialog/form/button` could generate a Playwright locator string of `get_by_role("button", name="Login")`.

title: Fix: Properly await LLM connection verification before agent run
body:
<!-- This is an auto-generated description by mrge. -->
## Summary by mrge
Fixed a critical issue where the agent would fail at startup due to unverified LLM connections. The asynchronous connection verification is now properly awaited before the agent begins operation, preventing premature failures.

**Bug Fixes**
- Fixed the LLM connection verification by properly awaiting it at the beginning of the agent's run method.
- Removed the non-awaited verification call from the initialization method that was causing a RuntimeWarning.

**Refactors**
- Moved connection verification to ensure it completes before any LLM-dependent operations begin.
- Replaced an assertion check with the actual verification process for more robust error handling.

<!-- End of auto-generated description by mrge. -->

## Description

This PR addresses an issue where the agent could fail immediately upon starting if the LLM connection verification hadn't completed. The `_verify_llm_connection` asynchronous function was called but not awaited before the main agent loop began in the `run` method.

This resulted in a `RuntimeWarning: coroutine 'Agent._verify_llm_connection' was never awaited` and could cause the agent to hit its `max_failures` limit without performing any actual steps, as the LLM calls would fail.

## Changes Made

 - Removed the non-awaited call to `_verify_llm_connection` from the `__init__` method of the `Agent` class.
 - Added `await self._verify_llm_connection(self.llm)` at the beginning of the `run` method in `browser_use/agent/service.py`.

## Impact

This change ensures the agent robustly verifies its connection to the LLM service *before* attempting any operations that require it, preventing premature failures and improving startup reliability.

title: Fix: Ensure first element is correctly indexed in sibling list
body:
<!-- This is an auto-generated description by mrge. -->
## Summary by mrge
Fixed the element position calculation in DOM tree building to correctly index the first element among siblings. This ensures accurate XPath generation by properly handling elements regardless of their position in the sibling list.

**Bug Fixes**
- Fixed indexing of the first element in sibling lists that was previously skipped or incorrectly calculated
- Added new `getElementPosition` function that correctly determines element position among siblings with the same tag name
- Improved handling of edge cases where an element is the only one of its type in the parent
- https://github.com/browser-use/browser-use/issues/853
- Better implementation than Open PR https://github.com/browser-use/browser-use/pull/744

**Refactors**
- Replaced previous sibling-traversal logic with a cleaner Array-based approach
- Changed position calculation to use direct children of the parent element, avoiding non-element nodes
- Implemented 1-based indexing for consistent XPath generation

<!-- End of auto-generated description by mrge. -->

#### **Overview:**
This update introduces a more reliable and efficient method for determining the position of an element among its siblings, specifically focusing on elements with the same tag name. The solution now properly accounts for the position of the **first element** and ensures correct indexing whether it's the first, middle, or last element of its type in the parent.

#### **Key Changes:**
- **Element Position Calculation:**
  - The `getElementPosition` function has been enhanced to correctly calculate the position of an element among its **direct siblings** with the same tag name.
  - The function now:
    - Filters siblings by tag name.
    - Returns `0` if the element is the only one of its tag type (first in the list).
    - Returns the **1-based index** of the element if multiple siblings share the same tag.
    - Ensures that the **first element** is also properly indexed (no longer skipped).

- **Parent Element Handling:**
  - Uses the parent’s direct children (via `parentElement.children`) to ensure the correct position within the sibling list.
  - This avoids counting non-element nodes (such as text nodes or comments), ensuring more accurate calculations.
  
- **Robustness:**
  - Returns `null` for cases where no siblings exist (i.e., the element has no siblings in the DOM).
  - Handles edge cases where the element might be the only one of its type in the parent.
  - Accounts for the first element, ensuring the position calculation begins correctly.

#### **Why This Change?**
- **Previous XPath Issue:**
  The previous approach to generating the XPath would resolve to multiple elements because it didn't correctly account for the position of the **first element** in the sibling list. This caused an issue where the XPath would resolve to more than one matching element, leading to errors like:
  ```
  Failed to locate element: Locator.element_handle: Error: strict mode violation: locator("html > body > div:nth-of-type(2) > div > div > main > div > div:nth-of-type(2) > div > div:nth-of-type(2) > div > div > div:nth-of-type(2) > div > div > div > div > div > div:nth-of-type(2) > div > div > div > div:nth-of-type(2) > div > div > div > div:nth-of-type(2) > div > button.Dniwja_spectrum-ActionButton.Dniwja_spectrum-BaseButton.Dniwja_i18nFontFamily.Dniwja_spectrum-FocusRing.Dniwja_spectrum-FocusRing-ring[type=\"button\"][aria-label=\"Add guideline\"][data-testid=\"content-popover-actionBtn\"]") resolved to 9 elements.
  ```

Earlier, the generated XPath looked like this:
```
html/body/div[2]/div/div/main/div/div[2]/div/div[2]/div/div/div[2]/div/div/div[2]/div/div/div/div/div/div[2]/div/div/div/div[2]/div/div/div/div[2]/div/button
```

After this change the XPath looks like below:

```
html/body/div[2]/div/div/main/div/div[2]/div/div[2]/div/div/div[2]/div/div/div[2]/div/div[1]/div/div/div/div[2]/div/div[1]/div/div[2]/div/div[1]/div[1]/div[2]/div/button
```

- With this change, the **correct 1-based position** of the first element is now properly considered, ensuring that the XPath or element locator resolves to a single, accurate element.

Fix AgentHookFunc type to be awaitable to correctly reflect usage of await on_step_start(self) and await on_step_end(self) in the agent service

Originally we had defined
AgentHookFunc = Callable[['Agent'], None]

However we had args of this type:
on_step_start: AgentHookFunc | None = None, on_step_end: AgentHookFunc 
Which we called like this:
if on_step_start is not None:
    await on_step_start(self)
if on_step_end is not None:
    await on_step_end(self)

So really the type should be awaitable
AgentHookFunc = Callable[['Agent'], Awaitable[None]]

This change clears up the linter error that was present in custom-functions\custom_hooks_before_after_step.py
And makes the usage of these hooks more clear
